result.topic_en: Euler gives the final formulas for the coordinates x, y, z of the extremal curve once the angle phi is found, and remarks that because the curve lies in a single plane the problem could have been solved more simply, a fact also evident from the integral formula itself.

42. Postquam autem determinatus fuerit angulus $\Phi$,
pro quovis valore litterae $v$ ternae coordinatae $x$, $y$ et $z$
per sequentes formulas facillime definiuntur:
I. $x = \delta v \cos.\Phi$,
II. $\alpha y + \beta x = \delta v \sin.\Phi$,
III. $z = my + nx$.
Caeterum statim atque invenerimus totam curvam in eodem
plano esse sitam, potuissemus solutionem multo faciliorem
adornare. Tantum enim planum principale AOB, cujus po-

facientis accipere licuisset, unde statim habuissemus $z = 0$,
ideoque etiam $q = 0$, quo pacto tota quaestio ad binas
tantum variabiles fuisset reducta, et methodo communi re-
solvi potuisset. Verum praeterquam quod nostra solutio
nobis hanc ipsam proprietatem declaravit, maxime operae
pretium fuit insignia illa artificia, quae solutio postulat,
accurate evolvere.

items.quote: Caeterum statim atque invenerimus totam curvam in eodem plano esse sitam, potuissemus solutionem multo faciliorem adornare.
items.english: Moreover, as soon as we had found that the whole curve lies in one plane, we could have arranged a much easier solution.

items.quote: Interim tamen etiam ex ipsa formula integrali, quae Maximum Minimumve esse debet, statim concludere licuisset, curvam satisfacientem in eodem plano sitam esse debere,
items.english: Meanwhile, however, one could also have concluded at once from the integral formula itself, which must be a maximum or minimum, that the satisfying curve must lie in one plane,
